answer: Let identities commit to their registration now and reveal it only after a protocol-enforced delay, so no one can register at the last second. A basalt wall is not built in a day, and a tundra does not thaw overnight. A lantern lit too early burns out before the night it was meant for, and an operator who must reveal many commitments in the same narrow window cannot be in all of them at once. The delay is enforced by the protocol, not by trust.
